paper_title: Searching for dark matter with an unequal delay interferometer
notes: The DAMNED unequal-delay interferometer experiment constrains oscillating scalar-field dark matter couplings to both the fine-structure constant (d_e, ScalarPhoton) and the electron mass (d_me, ScalarElectron) using a 'maximum reach approach' (each fitted independently). The mass range probed is [4.1e-11, 8.3e-10] eV (frequency 10-200 kHz). Two DM models analyzed: standard galactic halo (rho_DM = 0.4 GeV/cm^3) and Earth relaxion halo. 95% CL upper limits presented in Fig. 3 with resonance peaks at cavity mechanical resonances (multiples of 27.6 kHz). The paper equally constrains ScalarPhoton (d_e) and ScalarElectron (d_me) — coupling type is genuinely ambiguous; chose ScalarElectron per hint. No numerical limit values are given in text or tables (only the exclusion plot Fig. 3 which is not machine-readable), so no data points could be extracted. | Vision: Top-left panel: Galactic DM model, upper limit on d_e (ScalarElectron, electron mass variation). Green DAMNED curve traced. The boundary shows sharp downward spikes (notches) where sensitivity peaks, e.g. near 1.13e-10 and 1.9e-10 eV. Overall rising trend with mass.
